text: Which project brought historians of philosophy together with theoretical physicists to compare the conceptions of time in Plato and Kant with emergent time in quantum gravity and quantum cosmology?
reference_answer: PROTEUS (project 758145), 'Paradoxes and Metaphors of Time in Early Universe(s)'. It built a multi-disciplinary team of historians of philosophy, philosophers of physics and theoretical physicists to study how Western philosophy represents time in cosmology, examining the notions of time and the paradoxes arising in the philosophy and cosmology of Plato and Kant and setting them against the fundamental characters of emergent time in current quantum gravity and quantum cosmology. Its results include the digital archive 'Timaeus and Its Legacy', the COSMOS Network, and the edited volume 'Time and Timelessness in Fundamental Physics and Cosmology' (Springer 2024).

text: A research fellowship screened lakes spread along the whole length of Sweden for the fungi living in their water, identifying them from genetic traces in the samples because such organisms are hard to keep alive in a dish. Roughly what fraction of the fungal species it turned up had never been formally described?
reference_answer: About 25% - the CRYPTRANS fellowship reported that approximately 25% of the fungal species it detected in its lake survey were new, undescribed species still awaiting formal description and scientific recognition.

text: How do the projects whose central objective is to develop a cosmic-ray muon scanner for screening closed cargo containers and vehicles differ in what their scanners are built to detect?
reference_answer: Two projects have the muon scanner itself as their central objective, and they aim it at different threats. IMPRINT is built around the innovative Muon Detection System that Lingacom is developing, using high-energy natural atmospheric cosmic ray muon particles to look for high-Z materials used in nuclear bombs and shielded radioactive materials (used in 'dirty bombs') in containerized cargo and vehicles - the case where Radiation Monitors and X-ray fail on dense or high attenuating vehicles - and it reconstructs 3D imaging from muon data, with the aim of stopping insiders stealing material from nuclear and radioactive sites. SilentBorder develops and validates a cosmic-ray tomography (CRT) scanner for border guard, customs and LEAs whose target is much broader smuggling: hazardous and illegal goods (e.g. SNM), contraband such as tobacco or explosive, and hidden persons in up to 20' iso containers, exploiting the fact that cosmic-ray muons are highly penetrating, about 10,000 times the energy of a typical X-ray, to distinguish materials and give a visualised 3D image. So IMPRINT is a nuclear-security instrument narrowed to shielded high-Z material, while SilentBorder is a customs instrument that also has to find organic contraband and people.
notes: CRITERION (the discriminator, stated in the question text): the project's own central objective is to develop a cosmic-ray muon scanner for screening closed cargo containers and vehicles. IN 101021812 SilentBorder - 'The main objective of SilentBorder is to develop and validate a new high-technology CRT scanner for border guard, customs and LEAs'; the whole project is the scanner. IN 696945 IMPRINT - the project is Lingacom's 'innovative Muon Detection System for detecting high-Z materials ... in containerized cargo and vehicles', with objectives (2) 3D imaging software from muon data, (3) field test and demonstration, (4) commercialization of the IMPRINT product; the whole project is the scanner. OUT 786945 COSMIC - a Muon Scanner does appear in its text ('Muon Scanner (by Lingacom) for detection of shielded N&R (Nuclear and Radioactive) in dense containers, based on muon cosmic rays, for secondary inspection stage'), but it is one of eight new CBRNE sensors and COSMIC's own objective is 'a three stage (primary, secondary, focused manual inspection) detection system using new set of innovative sensors', so the muon scanner is a supplied component of a multi-sensor system, not the project's objective. OUT 883424 ENTRANCE - 'Muons Scattering Imaging in second line' is the third of three technologies combined for high-density iron ore cargo inside an NII toolbox (X-ray/deep learning, tagged neutron TNIS, photofission, passive RPM portal); its objective is 'an integrated toolbox for risk-based NII of cross-border cargo'. OUT 755371 CHANCE - it does build 'a suitable mobile muon detection system', but Muon Tomography is one of three characterization techniques (with calorimetry and Cavity Ring-Down Spectroscopy) and its target is 'the non-destructive interrogation of the content of large volume RW', i.e. conditioned radioactive waste packages destined for geological disposal, not cargo containers or vehicles; it fails both arms of the criterion.
